title: Modernize observability pipeline: swap sync harvester for event-driven collector and low-allocation span carrier
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Replace the existing synchronous metrics/trace harvester with an event-driven, non-blocking collector and introduce a low-allocation span carrier for cross-thread context propagation. This work targets CPU and P50 request latency regressions observed under high QPS that trace/metrics flushing causes. Scope: runtime agent (C++/Rust components), Go control-plane adapters, and the JVM ingestion shim used by some legacy services.
acceptance_criteria: Observability agent no longer performs long blocking flushes on request path (no blocking >10ms observed in flame graphs)
P50 tail latency for small text-gen (64 tokens) decreases by >=6% under 95th percentile load profile compared to baseline
CPU usage of runtime agent reduced by >=12% during synthetic load (same load harness)
Span and metric loss rate during rolling deploys remains <=0.05% and no data spikes in backlog metrics
All changes covered by CI smoke tests and e2e tracing validation; rollout gated by canary dashboard
implementation_notes: Introduce event queue with bounded ring buffer in runtime-agent (C++), coalescing metric deltas and using an async worker for batching to exporter clients
Replace sync histogram aggregator with async batcher (OpenTelemetry SDK upgrade to v1.21 for Go and Java instrumentation to pick up BatchSpanProcessor fixes)
Add low-allocation SpanCarrier object used by hot-path pathfinding code to avoid map allocations during context propagation (Go and Rust variants)
Refactor logging in agent from legacy fmt-based paths to zap with pooled buffers for high-throughput endpoints
Instrument adaptive batching heuristics: dynamic batch size tuned on token length distribution and current queue latency thresholds
Maintain a compatibility mode flag (agent.env OBS_COLLECTOR_MODE=compat) to revert to legacy sync harvester in emergencies
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Design sync meeting with runtime and infra; agreed on ring buffer approach and backpressure signals. Action: Aisha to prototype C++ ring buffer with single-producer/multi-consumer pattern.
2025-02-18: Prototype shows 28% lower allocation rate on hot path for small requests. Initial microbench results attached to PR.
2025-02-22: Upgraded Go OpenTelemetry SDK to v1.21 in a feature branch; fixed breaking changes for Resource detection. See PR #4679.

2025-02-24: Load test (k6 harness) against staging runtime with prototype collector: P50 latency improved 7.4% under 10k rps synthetic profile. CPU reduced by 14%. Collected flamegraphs: https://dashboards.internal.redwood/runtime/flame/ENG-213579-20250224
2025-02-26: Design review feedback from Jin Wei and Priya Sharma: add canary gate and metric for queue-saturation; avoid long lived locks in exporter path. Implemented changes in ring buffer code.
2025-02-28: End-to-end tracing validation failing intermittently due to a missing context propagation path in the JVM shim; created ENG-213880 to fix the JVM carrier. Will block rollout until fixed.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature branch behind feature flag (agent.env OBS_COLLECTOR_MODE=event).
2) Deploy to internal staging cluster; run k6 smoke profile; verify canary dashboard thresholds.
3) Enable in 5% of production traffic for 2 hours; monitor queue-saturation metric and span-loss rate.
4) If stable, ramp to 25% for 6 hours; then 100% over 24 hours. Emergency rollback path: set OBS_COLLECTOR_MODE=compat nationwide.
5) Post-mortem/template if any data gaps or latency regressions observed
test_plan: Unit tests for ring buffer and backpressure signals (C++/Rust)
Integration tests that validate no span loss when exporter endpoints are slow (CI job simulating 500ms exporter latency)
E2E tracing smoke test verifying trace integrity across the new SpanCarrier (job: e2e-tracing-suite)
Load tests (k6) run in staging: baseline vs event-driven collector comparisons documented in perf report
Chaos test: kill exporter worker threads and ensure graceful draining without blocking request threads
notes: We intentionally keep a small on-agent buffer TTL (200ms) to avoid unbounded memory growth in bursty traffic patterns.
Metric cardinality pruning rule added to limit label sets from user-provided metadata — see otel-config snippet in Confluence doc.
Follow-up: coordinate with platform team to deprecate legacy prometheus pushgateway adapter (ENG-214900 planned next quarter).
